decisions.statement: A plugin is read back only where the shell has every call this page states.
A plugin the shell does not have is read back as null rather than thrown over.
The device secret is presented by the native layer and answered with a status.
The device secret is never read back into JavaScript.
The response minting a device secret is the one place JavaScript sees the plaintext.
A presentation held false means the keychain answered with nothing.
A shell with no presentation never decides the held secret is bad.
A handover answers with a code and the verifier that code is bound to.

definition: the plugins the native shell puts on the window
